stage_prompts.prompt:
Use the provided image as the exact visual STYLE reference for a new gameplay-driven world design: bright refined low-poly 3D, crisp faceted green terrain and gray rocks, readable miniature architecture, turquoise water, soft light-blue space background, clean natural warm sunlight. Keep this charming low-poly aesthetic. Redesign the layout deliberately according to the management-game brief below.

Make a landscape 1536 x 1024 image, no UI and absolutely no text or symbols. One FULL spherical miniature planet is centered at about 48 percent of canvas width, 51 percent of height. Planet silhouette including terrain stays entirely inside the frame, approximately 820 pixels tall, with clear quiet margins on all four sides. Nearly orthographic elevated orbital management view. All facilities and trees orient upright to their local curved ground. Readable gameplay layout, no extreme perspective, no hero character, no spotlight on an individual citizen.

This is STAGE 1: THE FIRST RESOURCE-GATHERING SETTLEMENT. It must look like a playable management map with a small practical economy and plenty of land left to develop, NOT a planet filled with decorative cottages. Use the following permanent map anchors that will be retained in later eras:
- Upper left: one dense clearly bounded conifer forest reserve of roughly 16 low-poly trees, with a small logging worksite immediately at its FRONT edge. The worksite is an open wooden lean-to with an obvious log pile and stump, not a residential cottage.
- Upper right: a compact gray faceted rocky hill. At its front-left foot is an open STONE QUARRY with two shallow stepped cuts, distinct squared gray stone blocks and a simple wooden tool rack. No deep underground mine entrance yet.
- Center: ONE small central stockpile/common store, a very simple open timber shelter with clearly visible stacked logs, stone blocks, sacks and baskets on a clean packed-earth yard. This is the economy hub, larger than either house.
- Just behind the center: exactly TWO modest thatched huts grouped together, representing the housing capacity for a tiny population, with no additional scattered decorative houses.
- Mid-left below the forest: a very small berry-foraging patch, with low bushes carrying a few red berries and baskets. This is the initial food source. NO planted farms yet.
- Lower-left edge: ONE calm turquoise bay occupying about 15 to 20 percent of the visible hemisphere. A clean simple low-poly beige shoreline gently meets the blue surface. Water is a continuous smooth quiet surface following the globe, with two or three extremely subtle long pale streaks to suggest slow texture motion. No foam simulation, no crashing waves, no flowing rivers, no falls, no water spilling off cliffs, no whitewater, no bridges, no boats, no dock. Keep the same flat water level and simple shoreline.
- Mid-right and lower-right: generous OPEN buildable grassy land, so the player can expand toward farming, workshops and industry. Keep this empty visibly usable space. Low rounded terrain slopes permit construction; do not cover it with trees or huge mountains.

A very small number of narrow dirt paths connect the logging worksite, quarry, housing and berry patch TO the central stockpile. Every path must end at an actual worksite or building. Spatial grouping must explain resource collection and population allocation at a glance. Include at most six tiny ambient citizens working or carrying a resource as part of the automated settlement, no direct-control avatar. Tools, logs, stone and food baskets communicate functions through silhouettes. No metal smelter, no factory, no electric wires, no vehicles, no army, no towers, no ornamental park or random houses. No labels, arrows, HUD or text anywhere; these will be added separately. Prioritize logical functional design, restrained detail, clear spare land, robust low-poly geometry and a believable complete spherical world.

Edit the provided miniature planet into a later stage of THE SAME civilization-management game. Preserve its exact low-poly aesthetic, camera, full-globe composition, overall coastline, single lower-left calm bay, upper-left forest reserve and upper-right rocky hill. It should be recognizably the same planet after the player has developed it. Keep the full sphere visible. Bright faceted low-poly geometry, natural jade greens, warm ochre roofs, light-blue empty background, soft sunlight. Keep facilities useful and readable, with functional props and connected roads. All buildings align to local spherical ground. No isolated ornamental cottages, no purposeless roads, no hero, no direct-control character. Small citizens and vehicles are autonomous background workers. Do not cover the whole planet in construction; retain forest resources and a meaningful open buildable area.

Water design is deliberately feasible for a game: continuous calm blue water shell at a fixed level, a clean fixed shoreline, only a few long soft pale streaks to suggest slowly scrolling texture. No waterfalls, no cascade, no splashes, no elaborate animated foam, no breaking waves, no rivers cutting across steep mountains. Shoreline water must never fall down cliffs or spill off the sphere. A short shallow irrigation channel may be used only where explicitly requested below, running along a gentle contour with visible fixed channel borders.

Render WORLD ART ONLY. No interface, no text, no captions, no arrows, no labels, no badges, no typography, no giant holograms. We will add precise management UI and explanations separately. Every new building must have a clear function and recognizable tools or stored materials. No spaceships, no off-planet content, no satellites, no huge skyline. No vague futuristic monoliths. The development state is specified below.

STAGE 2: AGRICULTURE AND GROWTH. Keep the logging camp at the upper-left forest edge, the stone quarry at the upper-right hill foot, the central stockpile, and the existing housing location.

Develop the open grassy land just below and to the right of the central stockpile into THREE orderly cultivated plots, one golden wheat field and two green crop fields. Put a modest unmistakable timber granary with grain sacks directly BETWEEN these fields and the central store, reached by one short dirt road. A small practical TOOL WORKSHOP, an open-sided wooden shed with a workbench, axe heads and wooden handles, sits immediately right of the store and close to the stone and timber delivery path. Expand the existing two-hut housing group to FOUR compact thatched or simple wood houses only in the same small north-central residential cluster. Do not scatter housing around the globe.

Make the player choice readable: farms and granary support population growth; the tool workshop improves gathering and construction. Visible stored grain and tools emphasize their different functions. Retain a small berry patch as a basic fallback food source. One modest shallow timber-lined IRRIGATION DITCH starts at a simple intake at the calm bay edge and follows a short gentle contour to the nearest cultivated plot. It has a plain blue ribbon surface and only two or three pale lengthwise flow streaks. This is a cheap fixed-shape water channel, no splash or waterfall, no network of complex rivers, no waterwheel and no dam. Show one reserved empty grassy plot next to the fields for future expansion.

Paths connect every production building to the central stockpile and link housing to workplaces. A handful of tiny citizens and one handcart may illustrate automatic labor. No smelter, no metal mine tunnel, no electric power, no motors, no army. All facilities directly serve food, housing or tool technology. The bay, forest and hill stay in their original places.

STAGE 3: METALLURGY AND TECHNOLOGY. Keep a compact agricultural area of THREE cultivated plots in the lower-center/right area beneath the original stockpile, a small granary between those fields and the store, a housing cluster of four modest wood-and-stone cottages at the original housing location, and the logging camp at the same upper-left forest edge. Maintain the simple calm bay; preserve a short plain shallow field-side water ditch with no animated foam.

The main new feature is ONE clear ordered production corridor along the RIGHT side of the central hub, leading down from the original upper-right rocky hill: first an ORE MINE entrance with ore carts and rust-brown ore lumps at the hill foot; next, just below the mine, ONE compact brick SMELTING FURNACE with a small chimney, warm orange furnace opening and neatly stacked metal ingots; finally farther down the same short road ONE open-sided METAL TOOL WORKSHOP with anvils, workbenches, finished pickaxes and tool racks. Make these three facilities distinct in silhouette and position, with visible space between each. ONE ore cart on the upper road and ONE small ingot cart near the furnace make inputs and outputs legible. Preserve the older stone-cutting area as a small neighboring source of construction material.

Upgrade the CENTRAL STOCKPILE in place into a slightly larger storehouse with an organized outdoor yard displaying logs, food sacks and metal ingots in separate stacks. Add a very small RESEARCH ANNEX attached to the tool workshop, indicated by a drafting table with a blank pale blueprint, a simple cog model and a roof skylight, not by a grand library or decorative tower. No readable writing. New equipment is researched and manufactured in this practical workshop area. Keep the lower-right/front edge partly vacant for future industrial expansion. Roads explain the relationship mine to furnace to workshop to shared storage. No tanks, no electric grid, no spaceship, no full modern city.

STAGE 4: ELECTRIC INDUSTRY AND VEHICLE PRODUCTION, a later single-planet civilization stage. Retain the same forest reserve at upper left with an upgraded sawmill at its edge, the rocky resource hill at upper right, the calm lower-left bay, and recognizable older districts. Upgrade the compact north-central housing cluster in place to six modest low-rise brick apartment/workers houses. Keep three productive agricultural plots and a granary in the lower-left/center inland area, with a short shallow plain-blue irrigation ditch if it fits the established terrain. There are still forest resources, food production and small open grass areas; industry must not erase the economy that supports it.

Arrange a distinct purposeful INDUSTRIAL CORRIDOR on the right hemisphere: the ore mine remains at the hill foot; a brick smelter below it produces clearly visible stacked steel ingots; a machine-parts workshop below the smelter has gears and crates outside; a vehicle assembly hall farther down on the lower-right buildable area has a wide open assembly bay and an unfinished chassis visible inside. Each facility is separated by a short section of road and clearly identifiable by its work in progress.

Place ONE modest electricity GENERATOR STATION adjacent to the industrial zone with two small turbine housings, a transformer and a single restrained smokestack. A short, tidy run of three simple power poles connects the generator to the factory buildings. Do not cover the planet in cables. Two small low-poly trucks carry resources along the actual industrial road.

Immediately adjacent to the vehicle assembly hall, include a compact functional VEHICLE MUSTER YARD containing EXACTLY TWO small clearly readable olive-green tracked tanks and one low barracks/service shed. Tanks are the manufactured output and a managed squad, not decorative units sprinkled over the landscape; do not stage any battle. This military production competes for parts and electricity. Central storage upgrades in place into an organized warehouse with food crates, timber and metal stocks. A small research/engineering annex belongs to the machine workshop. No arbitrary castles, no residential skyscrapers, no airport, no rockets, no spacecraft, no extra planet.

Maintain low-poly game-ready forms and legible economic relationships: farms sustain population, resource sites feed industry, generator supplies factories, assembly produces trucks and tanks. Show concentrated districts and a coherent hierarchy instead of a random dense city. Keep the coastline and water simple and consistent with the reference.

water_material_edit:
Perform a precise LOCAL WATER MATERIAL revision of this civilization-management-game concept, using the provided mask. Preserve the entire planet geometry, camera, background, all buildings, facilities, people, roads, trees, farms, tanks, factory relationships and their exact positions. Keep the land terrain faceted low-poly.

Inside the existing calm blue bay, radically SIMPLIFY the water appearance into ONE smooth low-detail opaque turquoise surface following the planet. Use a softly graded clean blue-cyan base color with only TWO OR THREE very faint elongated soft turquoise highlight bands. Remove the mosaic of strongly contrasting triangular water facets, crystalline polygons, zigzag specular streaks and noisy little ripples. The water should look like a very simple clean game shader that can animate by slowly scrolling a soft texture. It is still obviously blue water, with gentle soft depth coloring and a stable simple shoreline. No glass crystals, no choppy waves, no storm, no splashes, no foam or physically simulated flow. Do not change the coastline or the world geometry. Keep the water surface calm and coherent.

If the selected small agricultural shore intake is visible, make it a compact static pump/intake box that connects to its fixed blue irrigation trough without an exposed falling-water spout. No waterfall. Preserve the simple blue channel and all nearby crops. Render no writing, no UI, no markers. Only refine the selected water material and selected intake area; all existing management facilities remain identical.
